chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The one who sits in the presence of the insulters of the Guardians of Allah, so he has disobeyed Allah the Exalted.

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءِ اللَّهِ: Guardians of Allah / Friends of Allah
key_terms.سَبَّابٍ: Insulter / One who curses or reviles

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on sitting with those who insult the Imams?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni uses this hadith to define 'sitting with' not merely as physical presence but as a form of tacit approval or companionship in sin, a concept central to Shia jurisprudence on social ethics. It underscores the principle of *al-Wala' wa al-Bara'* (loyalty and disavowal), where proximity to those who insult the Ahl al-Bayt is viewed as a spiritual deviation. This ruling serves as a practical guideline for maintaining religious identity in communal settings.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad in Abdul Jabbark, from Safwan, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who sits in the presence of the insulters of the Guardians<sup>asws</sup> of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, so he has disobeyed Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Exalted’.
en.sarwar: 14. Abu Ali al-Ash’ari has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘
Whoever sits with those who abuse the friends of Allah has certainly disobeyed Allah,the Most High.’”
